blocks.text: You can onboard Microsoft 365 (M365) tenants to DSPM to access Microsoft Information Protection (MIP) labels for Azure or on-premises Azure file shares.
Before onboarding an M365 tenant, make sure the following prerequisites are met:

blocks.item: You must be assigned either an Administrator role or a custom role with the Add SaaS Application permission.
Create and register an application and assign API permissions.
See instructions.
1. Create and register an application.
Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center or Azure portal and go to Microsoft Entra ID.
In the left-side navigation, go to Manage > App registrations.
Click + New registration.
See image.
On the Register an application page:
Name: Enter a unique name for the application.
Supported account types: Select the account types that can use this application from the drop-down menu.
Click Register.
See image.

The application is registered and details are displayed on the Overview page. Copy the Application (client) ID and save it. The client ID is required while updating the configuration details in the Zscaler Admin Console.
2. Assign API permissions.
In the All applications tab, click the newly created application.
In the left-side navigation, go to Manage > API permissions.
Click Add a permission.
See image.
In the Request API permissions drawer, assign the following API permissions:
Azure Rights Management Services
In the Microsoft APIs tab, select Azure Rights Management Services.
See image.
On the Azure Rights Management Services page, select Application permissions.
See image.
In the Select permissions list:
Under Application, select Application. Read.All.
Under Content, select Content.Writer.
Click Add permissions.
See image.
Microsoft Information Protection Sync Services
In the APIs my organization uses tab, search for Microsoft Information Protection Sync Service.
Select Microsoft Information Protection Sync Service from the search results.
On the Microsoft Information Protection Sync Service page, select Application permissions.
See image.
In the Select permissions list, under UnifiedPolicy, select UnifiedPolicy.Tenant.Read.
Click Add permissions.
See image.
Microsoft Graph
In the Microsoft APIs tab, select Microsoft Graph.
On the Microsoft Graph page, select Application permissions.
See image.
In the Select permissions list:
Under Application, select Application. Read.All.
Under InformationProtectionPolicy, select InformationProtectionPolicy. Read.All.
Click Add permissions.
See image.
The permissions appear in the Configured permissions list on the API permissions page.
Click Grant admin consent for <tenant name>.
In the Grand admin consent confirmation window, click Yes.
3. Generate the client secret or certificate.
Client secret
In the left-side navigation, go to Manage > Certificates & secrets.
In the Client secrets tab, click + New client secret.
In the Add a client secret drawer:
Description: Enter a description for the client secret.
Expires: Select the expiration time from the drop-down menu. By default, 180 days (6 months) is selected.
Click Add.
See image.
The client secret is generated and displayed.
Copy the secret immediately and save it for later use.
Certificate
Run any of the following commands in a CLI application:
To generate an encrypted file
To generate a certificate and a corresponding RSA private key:
openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -days 365 \ -keyout private.key \ -out certificate.crt \ -subj "/CN=my-sp-cert-password" \ -passout pass:<password>
To combine the private key and certificate into a single PEM file:
cat private.key certificate.crt > combined.pem
To generate an unencrypted file
To generate a private key (in 2048 bits) and save it to a specific file:
openssl genrsa -out <filename> 2048
To generate a self-signed X.509 certificate using an existing private key that is valid for 365 days:
openssl req -new -x509 -key <filename>.key -out <filename>.crt -days 365 -subj "/CN=<filename>"
To export the password for the newly created certificate:
openssl pkcs12 -export -out <filename>.pfx -inkey <filename>.key -in <filename>.crt
After you run the command, the following prompt appears:
Enter Export Password: Enter the export password
To convert the CRT file type to CER and upload to the Azure portal or Microsoft Entra admin center:
openssl x509 -in <filename>.crt -out <filename>.cer -outform DER
To create a PEM file from the CER file and upload it to the Zscaler Admin Console:
cat <filename>.key <filename>.crt > file.pem
In the Microsoft Entra admin center or Azure portal, click the newly created application.
In the left-side navigation, go to Manage > Certificates & secrets.
In the Certificates tab, click Upload certificate.
In the Upload certificate drawer:
Upload a certificate: Upload the CER certificate file from your local folder.
Description: Enter a description.
Click Add.
From the navigation menu, go to Data Security > DSPM > SaaS Applications.
On the SaaS Applications page, click Add SaaS Tenant.
The Add SaaS Tenant drawer appears.
In the Add SaaS Tenant drawer:
Tenant Type: Select Microsoft 365.
Tenant Alias: Enter a unique name for the tenant.
Tenant Name: Enter the name of the tenant.
Tenant ID: Enter the ID of the tenant.
Configuration Details:
Services: Select MIP Label.
Authentication Type: Select one of the following:
Client Secret
Enter the following information:
Client ID: The Application (client) ID you copied and saved from the Overview page in the Azure portal.
See image.
Client Secret: The client secret created for the app registration.
Client Certificate
Enter the following information:
Client ID: The Application (client) ID you copied and saved from the Overview page in the Azure portal.
Client Password: The export password for the certificate.
Certificate File: Upload the certificate file (PEM file) from your local folder or drag and drop the file.
See image.
Click Save.
The tenant is onboarded and is displayed on the SaaS Applications page.
